Grooms head buzzed. It happened around [Masha](http://ultraimg.com/images/bright_fairy_by_telthona-d89tzer.png) sometimes, then the forest looked different. Always the buzzing, made things look different. He couldn't quite figure it out. Maybe it was the new mushrooms. Masha had found a new type, she had told him, "be careful with these Groom, you cannot let them bloom"!

So Groom kept them small, which wasn't hard, since they were quite delicious. He had let one grow a bit, just to see. Then eaten it. He couldn't remember anything after that. Masha had woken him. It was the only time he had seen her angry, buzzing around like a nest of hornets! At least she hadn't set him on fire again, but now, he ate only the new mushrooms, never letting them grow.

She had threatened him too, Masha, so sweet, yet so scary. "Eat too many mushrooms again, I burn you again", she had said. She laughed when she said it, but her eyes, they never laughed. Groom noticed that much. So he hadn't contemplated the world since, just eaten the new baby mushrooms. Delicious, but no buzz.

She had gone missing once too, poor Masha. Groom had known something wasn't quite right. He had tried to shoo Masha before, but she had never left. He had even suggested outright, that she leave. But she had just laughed, and said to him, "but Groom, you are mine." So when she went missing, you would have thought, that Groom, would have been happy.

But, he hadn't been. Something sat wrong with him, like an uncomfortable truth, niggling at his bottom. So he had set off to find her, small, smiling Masha. Giggling, noisy, buzzing Masha. Oh, he had found her too, wrapped up in a spiders web. Surrounded by giant spiders. It had filled Groom with such anger. His poor Masha, being eaten. It was too much for him, he still felt bad about being angry. Poor spiders.

Groom had squished them, swinging his large, oaken hands, like great battering rams. Squish, squish, squish. And Masha had been okay too, which made Groom happy, but sad too, for the spiders. He had wanted so bad, after that, to find some red mushrooms. To contemplate what he had done. But Masha, had climbed up his back, and sung dawn songs in his ear. A great sadness had almost crushed him, but had left, when Masha was done.

She had called him her hero, "Groom, Oakenheart!" She had proclaimed him, but Groom had felt embarrassed about the whole thing. Masha had braided lantern vines, and carrion vines, onto his head, grafted them right in. Then had platted them, into a single warriors braid, as she had called it. Why did she always mock him, but Groom liked the new Vines, flowing down his back.

So it was, that Groom, with Masha, upon his shoulder, head still buzzing, stumbled upon something quite glorious. Groom had walked head first into a clearing, a clearing full of the most wonderful sight. There in the clearing, surrounded by Saen, was one he knew well. The big oak smiled, and said "Hello Saule!"

Mar'dy had been following the Saen since the ships landed. He said his farewells to the crew, and thanked them for their generosity. They had risked their lives to get them to this land. He wished he had something to give to them in return but he didn't, the captain too refused to take the sword. Though she was strong, the sword was too unwieldy for even her. When he suggested giving the vial to them, Saule reminded him:

"That vial is more of a burden than a gift. Don't draw so much attention to it."

Mar'dy agreed and they set off on their journey. It was a walk, not too strenuous though by the end of the day he was happy they didnt take the land route to the Tree of Life. On their occasional stops, Mar'dy pulled out two bark-bound journals that Saule made for him. In one he started to write his story and everything he had learned. In the other he started to write "On Arena Combat and Technique" where he went over every strategy he could think of for fighting. Just in case someone was interested, he supposed.

By the end of the day they met who Saule must have been looking for, another Saen. Mar'dy kept quiet during the interaction.

Masha buzzed around the clearing, so many new Saen to meet. Saen who had never met a Chlora! She danced around them, like a child at the fair. Smiling and giggling, delighting all. Even Diospyra smiled, though the sight of this creature, filled her with great sadness. But when Masha looked at Mar'dy, it filled him with unease, why he could not say.
